newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - EU clears merger of AXA, UAP.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU clears merger of AXA, UAP.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had cleared the merger between French insurance companies AXA SA and Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP).
The deal announced last month will create the world's second largest insurer after Japan's Nippon Life, with annual premium income of more than 300 billion francs ($57 billion).
At first sight the deal appeared to pose a threat to competition, but the Commission concluded that customers, especially corporate clients, would make sure this did not materialise.

"The Commission considers that the operation could create risks of a dominant position emerging but indicates that it has taken into account the capacity for customer demand to stimulate competition...as well as the presence of other competitors on the market," it said in a statement.
The Commission singled out rival companies Allianz of Germany and Italy's Assicurazioni Generali SpA as being capable of challenging the new French giant.
In a separate decision the Commission approved the acquisition by Generali of sole control of Prime SpA, an investment funds and life insurance unit of Italian car maker Fiat SpA.

In deciding on the AXA-UAP merger, the Commission also took into account the existence in France of mutual societies which, in recent years, have gained market share at the expense of insurance firms. AXA itself was a mutual society before becoming a global powerhouse.
In France and Belgium, UAP and AXA will together control about 15 percent of the whole insurance market, both in the life and non-life sectors, the Commission said.
The combined share would rise to about 30 percent in certain market segments such as civil liability, travel insurance and industrial accidents -- areas particularly targeted at business clients.

Earlier this month, AXA put its stamp on the deal which many market players say looks more like a takeover of UAP. In a clear signal of who will pull the strings, it said that the new group would use the name AXA worldwide.
AXA announced in November a share exchange offer for UAP which closed on Wednesday. The results will be known on January 13, but AXA has already said that the operation was "very successful".
